name: Salal

companions.note: Classic PNW understory pairing; similar light and moisture preferences
Native companion; both thrive in dry shade and support the same pollinator communities

pnw_notes: Native to Pacific Northwest coastal forests from Alaska to California. Extremely low maintenance once established — drought tolerant, deer resistant, and evergreen. Berries ripen August–September: mealy texture fresh, excellent for jams and drying. Historically one of the most important food plants for Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Coast. Takes 2–3 years to fully establish; slow to start, persistent once rooted. The leathery leaves are commonly used as florist greens.

planting_windows.notes: Fall planting preferred — cool, wet season aids establishment
Early spring planting also works before summer dry season
Berries ripe when dark blue-black; taste as you go — they vary by plant
